annotation.cut_point:
We are given a pricing structure for tickets at an amusement park:

- If you buy **up to 60 tickets**, the price per ticket is **\$70**.
- If you buy **more than 60 tickets**, the price per ticket is reduced by **\$1 for each additional ticket** you buy.

We are to find the **largest number of tickets $ t $** such that the **total profit is greater than \$4200**.

---

### Step 1: Define the price per ticket

Let $ t $ be the number of tickets bought in one order.

- If $ t \leq 60 $, then price per ticket is \$70.
- If $ t > 60 $, then the price per ticket is $ 70 - (t - 60) = 130 - t $.

So the price per ticket is:

$$
\text{Price per ticket} = 
\begin{cases}
70 & \text{if } t \leq 60 \\
130 - t & \text{if } t > 60
\end{cases}
$$

---

### Step 2: Define total revenue

Total revenue is:

$$
\text{Revenue} = t \times \text{Price per ticket}
$$

So:

$$
\text{Revenue} = 
\begin{cases}
70t & \text{if } t \leq 60 \\
t(130 - t) & \text{if } t > 60
\end{cases}
$$

---

### Step 3: Define profit

Let’s assume that **cost per ticket is fixed at \$50** (not given, but we can assume this for profit calculation).
